Q3.why: A hyperparameter table for the proposed method is a document-only step over settings the author already used.

Q4.why: Listing baseline hyperparameters means collecting settings from runs already made, with little new work, but a missing or contradictory baseline setting can cast doubt on fairness.

Q5.why: Releasing code takes cleanup and a repository, but it does not change the reported results.

Q6.why: Describing the search procedure is a paragraph, though an admitted small or ad hoc search can weaken trust in the gains.

Q7.why: Evaluating on unseen tasks or seeds needs new runs, and gains often shrink or vanish on held-out conditions.

Q8.why: Running a test is cheap on existing scores, but a non-significant comparison directly threatens the headline claim.

X2.why: Reporting error bars may need a few extra seeds, and wide intervals can blur the reported gap.

X3.why: Not selecting best runs only requires reporting all runs, but it can reveal that the reported best-case gain was optimistic.

X4.why: Giving baselines an equal tuning budget means re-running them, and a stronger tuned baseline often closes the reported gap.

X7.why: Stating total GPU-hours or equivalent is a sentence from logs the author already has.

Y1.why: Defining the measure (final, last-episode average, AUC, point of training) is a sentence, though a different definition could change the ranking.

Y5.why: Naming the codebase each baseline came from is a sentence or citation.

Y7.why: Giving environment or benchmark versions is a table entry from existing setup information.

Y8.why: A generalisation test outside training needs new environments or data and new runs, and often shows weaker transfer than the in-distribution claim.

Y9.why: A hyperparameter sweep needs many new runs, and sensitivity can show the gain holds only in a narrow range.

Y10.why: Listing software dependencies with versions is a read-off from the environment.

Y12.why: Tools such as rliable or performance profiles can be applied to existing scores, but they may show the gain is smaller or less certain than the mean suggests.
